t: For an additional amount for “Shipbuilding and Conversion, Navy”, $775,236,000, to remain available until September 30, 2010, for necessary expenses related to the consequences of Hurricane Katrina and other hurricanes of the 2005 season, which shall be available for transfer within this account to replace destroyed or damaged equipment; prepare and recover naval vessels under contract; and provide for cost adjustments for naval vessels for which funds have been previously appropriated: Provided, That this transfer authority is in addition to any other transfer authority available to the Department of Defense: Provided further, That the Secretary of Defense shall, not fewer than 15 days prior to making transfers within this appropriation, notify the congressional defense committees in writing of the details of any such transfer: Provided further, That the amount provided under this heading is designated as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 402 of H. Con. Res. 95 (109th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2006.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the advance written notification before transfers is a consultative step before a federal decision. That notification goes only to congressional defense committees, which are inside the federal government, so no outside party is involved. The rest of the section is an emergency appropriation with transfer authority and has no public comment, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense shall, not fewer than 15 days prior to making transfers within this appropriation, notify the congressional defense committees in writing of the details of any such transfer

opus.w: This section makes an appropriation with transfer authority. Its only procedural requirement is advance written notice to the congressional defense committees, which are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: the Secretary of Defense shall, not fewer than 15 days prior to making transfers within this appropriation, notify the congressional defense committees in writing of the details of any such transfer
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the requirement to notify the congressional defense committees in writing before making transfers counts as procedural participation. It doesn't: Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this notice never reaches anyone outside it.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to notify congressional defense committees before making certain fund transfers. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, notification to Congress is intra-governmental communication and does not constitute participation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense shall, not fewer than 15 days prior to making transfers within this appropriation, notify the congressional defense committees in writing of the details of any such transfer
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying congressional committees is a form of participation because it involves external oversight. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is *inside* the federal government, and reports or notifications to Congress are a common trap that results in a "No" label. There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
